hints: Focus on the strongest intermolecular force in each substance, since stronger forces mean a higher boiling point.
Remember that hydrogen bonding beats permanent dipole-dipole forces, which in turn beat London forces alone, and London forces grow with more electrons.
Look for the one pair where you go from a substance with hydrogen bonding to one with only weak London forces.
walkthrough:
**Recall what controls boiling point**

Boiling separates molecules, so you must overcome intermolecular forces. Stronger forces mean more energy needed, so a higher boiling point.

Useful strength order:
$$\text{hydrogen bonding} > \text{permanent dipole-dipole} > \text{London forces alone}$$

**Compare each pair by forces and size**

For similar types of force, a larger molecule with more electrons has stronger London forces and a higher boiling point.

Check for $\text{N-H}$, $\text{O-H}$ or $\text{F-H}$ bonds, these allow hydrogen bonding between molecules.

**Apply to the four pairs and decide**

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ is polar and larger than $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ can H-bond but $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$ cannot, and $\text{Ar}$ has more electrons than $\text{Ne}$. So in those three the second substance boils higher.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ can H-bond via $\text{N-H}$, while $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ has only London forces, so the second substance boils lower.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ is non-polar with only London forces, while $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ is polar with permanent dipole-dipole forces plus stronger London forces due to Cl. The second substance therefore has the higher boiling point.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$ cannot hydrogen bond between its own molecules, it has only dipole-dipole and London forces. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ has $\text{O-H}$ hydrogen bonding, which is much stronger, so the second substance boils higher.
options.C: Incorrect. Both $\text{Ne}$ and $\text{Ar}$ are noble gases with only London forces. $\text{Ar}$ has more electrons and a larger electron cloud, so its London forces are stronger and its boiling point is higher than $\text{Ne}$.
options.D: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ has $\text{N-H}$ bonds and forms hydrogen bonds between molecules. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ is a similar size but is non-polar with only weak London forces, so much less energy is needed to separate it and it has the lower boiling point.
